source:
@@U00219@@
What can be nicer on Sundays and holidays
than to talk of war or rumors of it,
while far off somewhere,
maybe in Turkey,
they're pounding each others’ heads together.
You stand at the window, draining your glass,
and watch bright ships sail downstream,
and then at twilight wend your way back home
and thank God for the blessings of peace.

@@U00221@@
Right you are! There I agree!
Let them bust each others’ heads and
turn the world all topsy-turvy, as long as we're
true to our good old German customs.

@@U00223@@
(To the CITIZENS’ DAUGHTERS.)

@@U00224@@
Mercy! Aren't we all decked out!
What fine young things you ladies look!
Who wouldn't love to win prizes like you?
Now, now, not so snooty!
It’s all right, believe me, dearies,
I know how to get you what you want.

@@U00226@@
Come, Agatha!
I refuse to be seen in public places
with these dreadful witches.
All the same, last Halloween
she showed me my future lover in the flesh.

@@U00228@@
She showed me mine in a crystal ball;
a soldier with all his bold comrades.
I look around for him everywhere,
and yet I never seem to find him.
translation:
@@U00219@@
周日和节假日还有什么比这更好的事情呢
而不是谈论战争或战争谣言，
当远离某个地方时，
也许在土耳其，
他们互相敲打对方的头。
你站在窗前，喝干你的玻璃杯，
并观看明亮的船只顺流而下，
然后在黄昏时分踏上回家的路
并感谢上帝赐予和平的祝福。

@@U00221@@
你是对的！我同意！
让他们互相打爆对方的头
只要我们还在，世界就会变得天翻地覆
忠实于我们古老的德国习俗。

@@U00223@@
（致公民的女儿们。）

@@U00224@@
怜悯！我们还不是都装出来了！
你们女士们看上去多么年轻啊！
谁不想像你一样赢得奖品？
现在，现在，不要那么傲慢了！
没关系，相信我，亲爱的，
我知道如何让你得到你想要的东西。

@@U00226@@
来吧，阿加莎！
我拒绝出现在公共场所
和这些可怕的女巫在一起。
尽管如此，去年万圣节
她向我展示了我未来的情人的真身。

@@U00228@@
她给我看了我的水晶球；
一名士兵和他所有勇敢的战友。
我到处寻找他，
但我似乎从未找到过他。
